content:
Partition \(\{1,2,\dots,100\}\) into chains by grouping numbers with the same odd part. There are 50 odd numbers, hence 50 chains. In each chain, every smaller element divides the larger ones, so at most one element can be chosen from each chain. Thus the subset has size at most \(50\).

The set \(\{51,52,\dots,100\}\) has \(50\) elements, and no element divides another because any multiple of a number \(>50\) is at least \(102>100\).

\[
\boxed{50}
\]
